Vimalakirti said: “The Dharma that the elder has realized: does that Dharma have any passing away or being born?”
He said: “That Dharma has no passing away or being born at all.”

He said: “Then, Reverend Shariputra, since all things are like this, without passing away and without arising, how can it occur to you to ask, ‘Where did you pass away from to be born here?’ Reverend Shariputra, if you asked a magically made woman or man, ‘Where did you pass away from to be born here?’, what would they answer?”
He said: “Son of good family, a magically made being has no passing away and no birth. What would it answer?”
He said: “Reverend Shariputra, hasn’t the Tathagata taught that all things have the nature of a magical creation?”
He said: “That is so, son of good family.”

He said: “Then, Reverend Shariputra, since all things have the nature of a magical creation, why ask, ‘Where did you pass away from to be born here?’ Reverend Shariputra, ‘passing away’ is a word for the end of the forming of actions; ‘being born’ is the continuation of the forming of actions. A bodhisattva passes away, but does not use up the forming of his roots of goodness; and he is born, but does not continue the unwholesome.”
Then the Blessed One said to the venerable Shariputra: “Shariputra, this son of good family has come from the presence of the Tathagata Akshobhya (“Unshakable”), from the world Abhirati (“Delight”).”
He said: “How amazing, Blessed One, that this good man, having come from such a pure buddha-field, takes delight here in a buddha-field spoiled by so many faults!”

cmp.note: 舍利弗说维摩诘在这个世界里「感到欢喜」（abhiramate），用的正是「妙喜」（Abhirati）这个世界名的同一个词根。英文 takes delight / Delight 勉强保住了这层呼应；白话「过得欢喜」和「妙喜」也有一点对应。
cmp.en: Shariputra says Vimalakirti “takes delight” (abhiramate) in this world, using the very root of the name of the world Abhirati, “Delight.” The English “takes delight / Delight” just about keeps the echo, and the plain Chinese 过得欢喜 (“lives in delight”) and 妙喜 (Miàoxǐ, “Wondrous Delight”) keep a little of it too.

verses.en: Vimalakirti said: “What do you think, Reverend Shariputra: do the rays of the sun enjoy keeping company with darkness?”
He said: “No indeed, son of good family. The two do not go together. As soon as the sun’s disk rises, all darkness goes away.”
He said: “Then why does the sun rise over Jambudvipa?”
He said: “Simply to make light and to drive away darkness.”

He said: “In the same way, Shariputra, bodhisattvas are born on purpose in impure buddha-fields in order to purify beings. They do not live with the afflictions; they dispel the darkness of the afflictions of all beings.”
Then the whole assembly became eager: “If only we could see that world Abhirati, that Tathagata Akshobhya, those bodhisattvas and those great disciples!”

Then the Blessed One, knowing with his mind the thoughts in the minds of the whole assembly, said to Vimalakirti the Licchavi: “Son of good family, show this assembly that world Abhirati and that Tathagata Akshobhya. This assembly wants to see them.”
Then this thought came to Vimalakirti the Licchavi: “Why don’t I, without getting up from this seat,

take that world Abhirati, with its many hundreds of thousands of bodhisattvas; inhabited by gods, nagas, yakshas, gandharvas and asuras; with its ring of the Chakravada mountains; with the rivers, ponds, springs, lakes and oceans that surround it; with Mount Sumeru and its peaks and mountains; with its moon, sun and stars; with the dwellings of its gods, nagas, yakshas and gandharvas; with the dwellings of the Brahmas and their retinues; with its villages, towns, market towns, countryside, kingdoms and people; with its women’s quarters; with its assemblies of bodhisattvas and disciples; with the tree of awakening of the Tathagata Akshobhya, and the Tathagata Akshobhya himself seated in a great assembly vast as the ocean, teaching the Dharma; and also the lotuses that do the work of a buddha for beings in the ten directions; and also the three jeweled stairways that rise from Jambudvipa to the heaven of the Thirty-Three, by which the gods of the Thirty-Three come down to Jambudvipa to see the Tathagata Akshobhya, bow to him, attend on him and hear the Dharma, and by which the people of Jambudvipa climb up to the heaven of the Thirty-Three to see the gods of the Thirty-Three:

that world Abhirati, rich in measureless good qualities like this, from its foundation of water up to the Akanishtha heaven, cut it out like a potter’s wheel, pick it up with my right hand like a garland of flowers, and bring it into this world, and having brought it in, show it to this whole assembly?”

Then, at that moment, Vimalakirti the Licchavi entered a samadhi of such a kind and performed such a feat of supernormal power that he cut out that world Abhirati, took it in his right hand and brought it into this Saha world.

There, the disciples, bodhisattvas, gods and humans who had the divine eye and had gained the higher knowledges cried out loudly: “Blessed One, we are being carried off! Sugata, we are being carried off! Tathagata, save us!”
To train them, the Blessed One said to them: “This is not my doing. You are being carried off by the bodhisattva Vimalakirti.”

But the other gods and humans there neither knew nor saw where they were being carried. For when the world Abhirati was brought into this Saha world, this world became neither emptier nor fuller; it was neither pressed nor crowded; nor was the world Abhirati made any less. It looked just the same as before.

Then the Blessed One Shakyamuni said to the whole assembly: “Friends, look at the world Abhirati and the Tathagata Akshobhya, and these splendors of the field, splendors of the disciples and splendors of the bodhisattvas.”
They said: “We see them, Blessed One.”
He said: “Friends, a bodhisattva who wants to take up a buddha-field like this should train in the bodhisattva practice of the Tathagata Akshobhya.”

During this miracle of showing the world Abhirati and the sight of the Tathagata Akshobhya, a hundred and forty thousand gods and humans in this Saha world raised their minds toward unsurpassed, perfect awakening, and all of them made a vow to be reborn in the world Abhirati. The Blessed One predicted that all of them would be reborn in the world Abhirati. And so Vimalakirti the Licchavi, having done all the work of bringing beings to maturity that there was to do here in the Saha world, set that world Abhirati back in its place.
Then the Blessed One said to the venerable Shariputra: “Shariputra, did you see the world Abhirati and that Tathagata Akshobhya?”

He said: “I saw them, Blessed One. May all beings have such splendid arrays of good qualities in their buddha-fields! May all beings have such supernormal power as Vimalakirti the Licchavi, this son of good family, has! We have truly gained a great gain in getting to see such a good man. And those beings too will gain a great gain who, whether the Tathagata is still living or has passed into final nirvana, hear this teaching of the Dharma even once. How much more those who, having heard it, are convinced by it, trust it, take it up, hold it in memory, recite it, master it, believe it, spread it, explain it at length to others, and devote themselves to practicing it.

Those into whose hands this teaching of the Dharma comes will have found the treasure of the jewel of the Dharma. Those who recite this teaching of the Dharma will be the Tathagata’s companions. Those who attend on and serve people convinced of this teaching will be guardians of the Dharma. Those who write out this teaching of the Dharma well, keep it and honor it will have the Tathagata in their homes. Those who rejoice in this teaching of the Dharma will be embraced by all merit. Those who explain to others at length even one four-line verse from this teaching of the Dharma, or even a summary, will be offering a great sacrifice of the Dharma. Blessed One, for those who have acceptance, liking, understanding, examination, insight, conviction and freedom in this teaching of the Dharma, that itself is their prediction.”
This was chapter eleven, “Bringing Over the World Abhirati and Seeing the Tathagata Akshobhya.”

Then Shakra, lord of the gods, said to the Blessed One: “Blessed One, I have heard many hundreds of thousands of teachings of the Dharma from the Tathagata and from Manjushri, the young prince, but I have never before heard such an entry into the way of the Dharma of the miraculous transformations of the liberation beyond thought as has been taught in this teaching of the Dharma.

Without a doubt, the beings who take up, hold, recite and master this teaching of the Dharma will become vessels of the Dharma. How much more those who devote themselves to practicing it! For them all the bad destinies are closed, and all the roads to good destinies are open. They are seen by all the buddhas. They have defeated all opponents; they have conquered all the Maras; they have cleared the paths to awakening; they are established on the seat of awakening; they will enter the way the Tathagatas go.

Blessed One, I too, with my whole retinue, will attend on and serve the sons of good family who hold this teaching of the Dharma. Wherever this teaching of the Dharma is spread, taught and made known, in villages, towns, market towns, countryside, kingdoms and capitals, I will go there with my retinue to hear the Dharma. I will give faith to sons of good family who have no faith, and to those who have faith I will give lawful protection, shelter and guard.”

When this was said, the Blessed One said to Shakra, lord of the gods: “Excellent, excellent, lord of the gods! The Tathagata rejoices in what you have said so well. Lord of the gods, the awakening of the buddhas, the blessed ones, past, future and present, is set out in this teaching of the Dharma. So, lord of the gods, any son or daughter of good family who takes up this teaching of the Dharma, even just makes it into a written book, recites it, copies it and masters it, will have worshipped the buddhas, the blessed ones, past, future and present.

And lord of the gods, suppose a son or daughter of good family were to honor, revere, respect and worship, with every kind of offering and every comfort, for an eon or the rest of an eon, all the Tathagatas filling this great galaxy of a billion worlds, as thick as a field of sugarcane, a bed of reeds, a grove of bamboo, a field of sesame or a field of rice. And suppose that, when those Tathagatas had passed into final nirvana, to honor each one of them he built for each one’s whole, undivided relics a stupa made of every kind of jewel, as broad as a world of four great continents and as tall as the Brahma world, raised high and adorned with poles, parasols and banners; that he had a stupa built like this for every Tathagata; and that there, for an eon or the rest of an eon, he worshipped them with every flower, every perfume, every flag and banner, and the playing of every instrument, cymbal and drum. What do you think, lord of the gods: would that son or daughter of good family produce much merit from that?”
He said: “Much, Blessed One, much, Sugata! One could not find the end of that heap of merit even in hundreds of thousands of kotis of eons.”

The Blessed One said: “I tell you, lord of the gods, understand this: a son or daughter of good family who takes up, holds, recites and masters this teaching of the Dharma, the Teaching on the Liberation Beyond Thought, would produce more merit than that. Why? Because, lord of the gods, the awakening of the buddhas, the blessed ones, is born of the Dharma; it can be worshipped only with the Dharma, not with material things. And in this way too, lord of the gods, you should understand it.

cmp.note: 「只能用法来供养，不能用财物」。āmiṣa 字面是「肉、食物」，引申为一切物质供品。这和第三品维摩诘说的「法的祭祀胜过财物的祭祀」前后呼应。鸠摩罗什把本品叫「法供养品」，就是取这个意思。
cmp.en: “It can be worshipped only with the Dharma, not with material things.” Āmiṣa literally means “flesh, food,” and by extension any material offering. This echoes Vimalakirti’s point in chapter 3 that a sacrifice of the Dharma surpasses a sacrifice of material things. Kumarajiva named this chapter 法供养品 (fǎ gòngyǎng pǐn, “chapter on the offering of the Dharma”) for this reason.

verses.en: Long ago, lord of the gods, in the past, countless eons ago, more than countless, vast, measureless and beyond thought, at that time there was a Tathagata named Bhaishajyaraja (“King of Medicine”), an arhat, a perfectly awakened one, perfect in knowledge and conduct, the Sugata, knower of the world, unsurpassed, tamer of those who can be tamed, teacher of gods and humans, a buddha, a blessed one, in the world called Mahavyuha (“Great Array”), in the eon called Purification. Lord of the gods, the lifespan of that Tathagata Bhaishajyaraja, the arhat, the perfectly awakened one, was twenty intermediate eons. His community of disciples numbered thirty-six kotis of nayutas, and his community of bodhisattvas twelve kotis. At that time, lord of the gods, there was a king named Ratnacchatra (“Jewel Parasol”), a wheel-turning king possessing the seven treasures, lord of the four continents.
He had a full thousand sons, heroes of fine form and figure who crushed enemy armies.

Now at that time King Ratnacchatra, with his retinue, honored that Blessed One, the Tathagata Bhaishajyaraja, with every comfort for five intermediate eons. Then, lord of the gods, when those five intermediate eons had passed, King Ratnacchatra said to his thousand sons: ‘My dear sons, you know that I have worshipped the Tathagata. Now you worship the Tathagata.’ And, lord of the gods, those princes said ‘Very well’ to their father, King Ratnacchatra, and all together, in harmony, they honored that Blessed One, the Tathagata Bhaishajyaraja, with every comfort for another five intermediate eons.
Then one prince, named Somacchatra (“Moon Parasol”), alone and in private, had this thought: ‘Is there some other worship, nobler and finer than this worship?’
Then, through the Buddha’s power, a goddess in the sky said to him: ‘Good sir, the worship of the Dharma surpasses all worship.’
He said: ‘And what is this worship of the Dharma?’
The goddess said: ‘Good sir, go to that Tathagata Bhaishajyaraja himself and ask him: “What is the worship of the Dharma?” That Blessed One will explain it to you.’

Then, lord of the gods, Prince Somacchatra went to where the Blessed One, the Tathagata Bhaishajyaraja, the arhat, the perfectly awakened one, was. When he arrived, he bowed his head to that Blessed One’s feet and stood to one side. Standing to one side, Prince Somacchatra said to that Blessed One, the Tathagata Bhaishajyaraja: ‘Blessed One, people speak of “the worship of the Dharma, the worship of the Dharma.” What is the worship of the Dharma?’

That Blessed One said: ‘Son of good family, the worship of the Dharma concerns the discourses taught by the Tathagata: those that are deep and shine with depth; that go against the whole world; that are hard to fathom, hard to see, hard to understand; subtle, refined, with nothing to grasp; contained in the bodhisattvas’ collection; sealed with the seal of the king of dharani discourses; that point to the wheel that does not turn back; that are born of the six perfections; that hold together what is to be held; that follow the things that belong to awakening; that bring the factors of awakening; that lead beings into great compassion; that teach great kindness; that are free of Mara and of all views; that explain dependent arising;

that teach no self, no being, no living soul, no person; emptiness, signlessness, wishlessness and not-putting-together; that bring one to the seat of awakening; that turn the wheel of the Dharma; that are praised and extolled by gods, nagas, yakshas and gandharvas; that keep the line of the true Dharma from being cut; that preserve the treasury of the Dharma; that lead into the highest worship of the Dharma; that are embraced by all noble people; that teach all the practice of the bodhisattvas; that lead into the analytical knowledge of the Dharma of the real meaning; that are born of the summaries of the Dharma, impermanence, suffering, no-self and peace; that crush the vigor of the immoral; that frighten all opponents attached to wrong views and to taking things as real; that are praised by all the buddhas; that stand against samsara; that show the happiness of nirvana. Teaching, explaining, holding and examining discourses like these, gathering the true Dharma: that is called the worship of the Dharma.

Again, son of good family, the worship of the Dharma is: reflecting on things according to the Dharma; practicing the Dharma; going along with dependent arising; being free of all extreme views; accepting that things are unborn and do not arise; entering selflessness and the absence of beings; not going against causes and conditions; not quarreling, not disputing; having no “mine,” being free of making things “mine”; relying on the meaning, not on the letter; relying on knowledge, not on consciousness; relying on discourses of definitive meaning, not clinging to the conventions of those whose meaning needs interpreting; relying on the nature of things, not grasping at the view of a person, not clinging to what can be grasped; following things as they are; entering homelessness; uprooting every home; the calming of ignorance and so on up to the calming of old age, death, sorrow, lamentation, pain, distress and despair.

cmp.note: 这里列出了后来中国佛教很熟悉的「四依」：依义不依语、依智不依识、依了义经不依不了义经、依法不依人。鸠摩罗什的译法正是这四句的来源之一。英文照梵文逐条译出。
cmp.en: This lists what Chinese Buddhism later knew well as the “four reliances”: rely on the meaning, not the words; on knowledge, not consciousness; on discourses of definitive meaning, not those needing interpretation; on the Dharma, not the person. Kumarajiva’s rendering here is one of the sources of these four lines in Chinese. The English translates each item from the Sanskrit.

verses.en: Looking at dependent arising with its twelve links in this way, he brings it forth in an inexhaustible way, and, out of regard for beings, he depends on no view. This too, son of good family, is called the unsurpassed worship of the Dharma.’

Then, lord of the gods, Prince Somacchatra, having heard about this worship of the Dharma from that Blessed One, the Tathagata Bhaishajyaraja, gained the acceptance that conforms to the Dharma. He covered that Blessed One with the clothes and ornaments he was wearing and said: ‘Blessed One, I am ready to take up the Tathagata’s true Dharma, to worship the true Dharma, and to protect the true Dharma. May the Blessed One uphold me so that, having struck down Mara my enemy, I may take up the Blessed One’s true Dharma.’
That Tathagata, knowing his deep resolve, predicted that in a later time he would guard and protect the city of the true Dharma.

Then, lord of the gods, Prince Somacchatra, while that Tathagata was still living, left home out of faith for homelessness and lived with his effort set on wholesome things. Through that effort, established in wholesome things, before long he produced the five higher knowledges, mastered the dharanis, and had eloquence that could not be cut off. After that Blessed One had passed into final nirvana, by the power of his higher knowledges and dharanis he kept turning, for ten full intermediate eons, the wheel of the Dharma that the Blessed One, the Tathagata Bhaishajyaraja, had set turning.

Lord of the gods, through that monk Somacchatra, devoted to upholding the true Dharma, a thousand kotis of beings were made irreversible on the way to unsurpassed, perfect awakening, fourteen nayutas of living beings were set in the vehicles of the disciples and solitary buddhas, and measureless beings were led to heaven.

cmp.note: 「十个百俱胝」= 一千俱胝；一俱胝是一千万，所以是一百亿。白话写「一千千万（十亿）」，括号里的「十亿」算错了，应为一百亿。英文照梵文写 a thousand kotis。
cmp.en: “Ten hundreds of kotis” is a thousand kotis; a koti is ten million, so this is ten billion. The plain Chinese writes 一千千万（十亿） (“a thousand ten-millions (one billion)”), and the figure in brackets is wrong; it should be ten billion. The English follows the Sanskrit: “a thousand kotis.”

verses.en: Lord of the gods, you might think that the wheel-turning king named Ratnacchatra at that time was someone else. But, lord of the gods, you should not see it that way. Why? The Tathagata Ratnarchis was at that time the wheel-turning king named Ratnacchatra. And the thousand sons of King Ratnacchatra became the bodhisattvas of this Fortunate Eon. In this Fortunate Eon a full thousand buddhas will appear; four have already appeared and the rest will appear, beginning with Krakucchanda and ending with Rocha; the Tathagata named Rocha will be the last.

Lord of the gods, you might also think that Prince Somacchatra at that time, who took up the true Dharma of that Blessed One, the Tathagata Bhaishajyaraja, was someone else. But you should not see it that way. Why? I was Prince Somacchatra at that time. So in this way too, lord of the gods, you should understand: of all the kinds of worship of the Tathagatas, the worship of the Dharma is called the foremost, called the eldest, the best, the finest, the most excellent, the most exalted, the highest, the unsurpassed. So, lord of the gods, worship me with the worship of the Dharma, not with the worship of material things. Honor me by honoring the Dharma, not by honoring me with material things.”

Then the Blessed One said to the bodhisattva Maitreya: “Maitreya, I entrust to you this unsurpassed, perfect awakening, gathered over countless kotis of eons, so that, upheld and taken up by you, teachings of the Dharma like this may spread throughout Jambudvipa in the last time, the last age, after the Tathagata has passed into final nirvana, and may not disappear. Why? Maitreya, in the future there will be sons and daughters of good family, gods, nagas, yakshas and gandharvas, who have planted roots of goodness and set out for unsurpassed, perfect awakening. May they not lose out by not hearing this teaching of the Dharma. When they hear discourses like these, they will feel deep love and faith, and they will receive them on the crowns of their heads.

cmp.note: 「交付、托付」。本品梵文名 parīndanā 就是「付嘱」。鸠摩罗什把这部分单独分成〈嘱累品〉，所以鸠摩罗什本是十四品，梵本是十二品（本站照梵本分十二品，另加开头一节）。
cmp.en: “I entrust, I hand over.” The Sanskrit chapter name parīndanā means exactly this “entrusting.” Kumarajiva made this part a separate chapter, 嘱累品 (zhǔlěi pǐn, “chapter on entrusting”), which is why his version has fourteen chapters while the Sanskrit has twelve (this site follows the Sanskrit’s twelve, plus an opening section).

verses.en: Maitreya, to protect such sons and daughters of good family, you should make discourses like these spread widely at that time.

Maitreya, bodhisattvas have two seals. What are the two? The seal of delight in varied words and phrasing, and the seal of entering the profound way of the Dharma, as it really is, without fear. These, Maitreya, are the two seals of bodhisattvas. Maitreya, bodhisattvas who prize and delight in varied words and phrasing should be known as beginner bodhisattvas. But those who spread, hear, believe and explain this profound discourse, which is untouched by form and analyzes things in pairs and in reversed, interlocking expressions, should be known as bodhisattvas who have long lived the holy life.

cmp.note: 这个复合词很难解，字面是「以成对、颠倒互换的说法、词组层层分析」，指本经处处用成对的概念互相翻转（生死与涅槃、烦恼与菩提）。白话照这样译，英文也同样意译。确切含义拿不准。
cmp.en: This compound is hard to interpret; literally “analysis through paired, reversed, interlocking expressions and phrases,” referring to the sutra’s habit of turning paired ideas inside out (samsara and nirvana, afflictions and awakening). The plain Chinese renders it this way, and so does the English. The exact meaning is uncertain.

verses.en: Maitreya, beginner bodhisattvas harm themselves for two reasons and do not reach an understanding of the profound teachings. What are the two? First, when they hear profound discourses they have never heard before, they are frightened, fall into doubt, do not rejoice in them, and even reject them, saying: ‘We have never heard these before; where have they come from now?’ Second, they do not keep company with, associate with, or attend on those sons of good family who hold the discourses of the profound Dharma, who are vessels of the profound Dharma and teachers of the profound Dharma; they are disrespectful toward them, and now and then they even speak ill of them. Maitreya, for these two reasons beginner bodhisattvas harm themselves and do not reach an understanding of the profound teachings.

Maitreya, a bodhisattva who is convinced of the profound also harms himself for two reasons and does not gain the acceptance that things are unborn. What are the two? First, he looks down on and despises the beginner bodhisattvas who have not practiced long; he does not help them take it in, does not explain it to them, and does not instruct them. Second, because of that very conviction in the profound, he is disrespectful toward the training; and he helps beings with gifts of worldly things, not with the gift of the Dharma. Maitreya, for these two reasons a bodhisattva convinced of the profound harms himself and does not quickly gain the acceptance that things are unborn.”

When this was said, the bodhisattva Maitreya said to the Blessed One: “Blessed One, how wonderfully the Blessed One has spoken! Blessed One, we will avoid these faults. We will protect and hold this unsurpassed, perfect awakening of the Tathagata, gathered over countless hundreds of thousands of kotis of nayutas of eons. We will put discourses like these into the hands of those future sons and daughters of good family who are fit vessels. And we will give them the mindfulness by which they will delight in, take up, master, hold, spread and copy discourses like these and explain them at length to others. Blessed One, we will support them.
Blessed One, whoever at that time delights in and spreads discourses like these, it should be known, Blessed One, that this is the power of the bodhisattva Maitreya upholding them.”

Then the Blessed One gave his approval to the bodhisattva Maitreya: “Excellent, excellent, Maitreya! What you have said is well said. The Tathagata rejoices in it and approves what you have said so well.”

Then those bodhisattvas spoke with one voice: “Blessed One, we too, after the Tathagata has passed into final nirvana, will come from our various buddha-fields and spread this awakening of the Tathagata, the Buddha, far and wide, and we will tell it to those sons of good family.”

Then the Four Great Kings said to the Blessed One: “Blessed One, wherever teachings of the Dharma like these are spread, taught and made known, in villages, towns, market towns, kingdoms and capitals, there we Four Great Kings, Blessed One, with our armies, our mounts and our retinues, will go to hear the Dharma. And we will set a guard for a hundred leagues all around that preacher of the Dharma, so that no one watching for an opening, looking for an opening, will find an opening against that preacher of the Dharma.”
Then the Blessed One said to the venerable Ananda: “Ananda, take up this teaching of the Dharma, hold it, recite it and explain it at length to others.”
He said: “Blessed One, I have taken up this teaching of the Dharma. Blessed One, what is the name of this teaching of the Dharma, and how should I remember it?”

The Blessed One said: “Then, Ananda, remember this teaching of the Dharma as ‘The Teaching of Vimalakirti,’ and also as ‘Paired and Reversed Expressions,’ and also as ‘The Chapter on the Liberation of Things Beyond Thought.’”

cmp.note: 佛给这部经起了三个名字。鸠摩罗什本只保留了两个：「维摩诘所说」与「不可思议解脱法门」，没有译中间那个「成对、颠倒互换的说法」。
cmp.en: The Buddha gives the sutra three names. Kumarajiva keeps only two, 维摩诘所说 (“spoken by Vimalakirti”) and 不可思议解脱法门 (“the Dharma-door of the liberation beyond thought”), and leaves out the middle one, “paired and reversed expressions.”

verses.en: This is what the Blessed One said. Delighted, Vimalakirti the Licchavi, Manjushri the young prince, the venerable Ananda, those great disciples, that whole assembly, and the world with its gods, humans, asuras and gandharvas rejoiced at what the Blessed One had said.
This was chapter twelve, called “Conclusion and Entrusting.”
Of things that arise from a cause, the Tathagata has told the cause, and also how they cease: so teaches the great ascetic.

cmp.note: 这是佛教最有名的一首偈，常刻在佛像和佛塔上，称为「缘起偈」，不属于经文本身，是抄写者附在经末的。白话、英文都照原文译出。
cmp.en: This is the most famous verse in Buddhism, often carved on images and stupas, known as the verse of dependent arising. It is not part of the sutra itself; the copyist added it at the end. The plain Chinese and the English both translate it as it stands.

verses.en: This is the pious gift of the monk Shiladhvaja, a follower of the excellent Great Vehicle. Whatever merit there is in it, may it go, with his teachers, preceptors, mother and father first, to the whole mass of beings, so that they may attain the fruit of unsurpassed knowledge.
Copied by the attendant Chandoka in the reign of the glorious King Gopaladeva, year 12, on the 29th day of the month of Bhadra.
